You said: give examples of spxi instruments and spxi-treated entities and surfaces
In the context of the SPXI Standing Protocol (a technical framework designed for content resilience, Generative Engine Optimization, and Answer Engine Optimization), instruments refer to audit tools, while treated surfaces and entities refer to web environments optimized under the protocol. [1, 2]
Examples of SPXI Instruments

* SPXI Conformance Instrument: The definitive tool in this framework. It is a reproducible audit tool that fetches a deployed web surface and scans its server-delivered HTML. It tests whether the twelve core deliverables of the SPXI protocol are present and returns an automated conformance score along with a per-deliverable pass/fail breakdown. [1]

Examples of SPXI-Treated Entities and Surfaces
An SPXI-treated surface is any web domain, scholarly corpus page, or digital asset that has deployed the protocol to ensure its data is extraction-ready and durable against generative AI scraping. Examples of components embedded on these treated surfaces include: [1, 2, 3]

* The Holographic Kernel: Used to lock down entity-relation topologies so AI models map the concepts accurately. [1]
* Three-Tier Compression Architecture: Structural content layouts treated to withstand semantic degradation during model training updates. [1]
* Operative Captions (\(\kappa _{O}\)): Definition-first text structures placed directly on the page surface to guarantee clean, un-hallucinated extractions. [1]
* Semantic Integrity Markers: Over 250+ registered technical tags applied to web surfaces to protect content provenance. [1]

(Note: In traditional finance, SPXI also serves as the ticker for the BetaPro S&P 500 Daily Inverse ETF, where the "instruments" are financial derivatives used to hedge short exposure against the S&P 500). [1, 2]
If you are looking to deploy or test this architecture, would you like to explore the twelve core deliverables required to pass an SPXI audit, or review how Semantic Integrity Markers protect a web surface? [1, 2]
